items.description: Lint gate: ESLint (flat config, typescript-eslint recommended) covers src/ and test/, provably lints the real files, the repo is lint-clean, and npm run verify runs typecheck + lint + tests.
steps: Add eslint and typescript-eslint as devDependencies with an eslint.config.js flat config covering src/**/*.ts and test/**/*.ts using the typescript-eslint recommended ruleset

Prove the linter bites: temporarily introduce an unused variable in a src file, run npm run lint, confirm it is flagged and that the reported linted-file count is nonzero, then revert the violation; record this evidence in .ralph/progress.md
Add script "lint": "eslint src test" and change "verify" to run typecheck, lint, and test
Run npm run lint, fix every finding in repo code without weakening any runtime behavior or test assertion (rule-level disables allowed only with a justifying comment)
Run npm run verify and confirm typecheck, lint, and the full vitest suite all pass

items.description: Rule matching and allow/deny composition: the bundled Policy Engine provider matches tool name, active provenance, and normalized input; deny beats allow; the outcome (decision, winning rule id, severity in the reason string) is deterministic regardless of rule order and object key order. Ask and hard-deny severities are NOT in scope here (items 4 and 5 own them).
steps: Write a failing test in test/policy-engine.test.ts at the direct dispatch seam (DefaultResourceLoader + createAgentSession + emitToolCall; reuse helpers from test/providers.test.ts): configure rules under providers[].config.rules per the plan's rule contract, emit a tool_call, and assert the block decision and that the reason carries the winning rule id and severity

Cover matching on tool name, provenance, and normalized-input matchers; deny-beats-allow composition; and determinism: identical decision, winning rule id, and reason with the rules array reordered and with object keys reordered; include a same-severity tie resolved by lexicographically smallest rule id
Run the tests, confirm red, summarize the red output in .ralph/progress.md

Implement src/policy-engine.ts as a config-driven provider on the events grant lane with a TypeBox configSchema for rules, bundle it in src/index.ts's default export (createPiHooksExtension({ providers: [policyEngineProvider] })), and run npm run verify green

items.description: Confirm-only interaction grant: a provider declaring the interaction grant can call confirm through a live-bound broker; when hasUI is false, confirm returns the caller-supplied noUiOutcome immediately without waiting; an undeclared provider's interaction access is refused via the existing refusal-proxy pattern with a grant-refused audit record.
steps: Write a failing test at the direct dispatch seam with a fixture provider declaring the interaction grant: with uiContext injected via session.bindExtensions({ uiContext }) reporting hasUI=false, confirm(request, { noUiOutcome: 'denied' }) resolves immediately to 'denied'; with hasUI=true and a stubbed ctx.ui.confirm, the stub receives the request and its answer is returned
Add a case where a provider without the interaction grant touches the interaction facade: refusal proxy throws and a grant-refused audit record is written (existing GRANT_KINDS refusal pattern)
Run red, record evidence in .ralph/progress.md

Implement the interaction grant kind in src/grants.ts + src/providers.ts and the broker in createHookHost (Host updates the broker's current DispatchContext per dispatch); extend DispatchContext.ui additively with confirm via one internal wider type for the Pi ui surface (the nine-event HookModule contract stays unchanged); run npm run verify green

items.description: Ask severity with fail-closed unattended safety: ask outranks allow in composition; with no UI an ask-matched tool_call resolves immediately to deny (fail-closed) and the tool never executes; with UI the session asks exactly once for the exact elevated action, allowing on accept and denying on reject.
steps: Write failing tests: at the direct dispatch seam, ask + allow rules matching together compose to ask (winning rule id and 'ask' severity in the reason) and resolve to a block when hasUI=false

At the scripted agent turn seam (deterministic session.agent.streamFn requesting a marker tool), prove the marker tool never executes under unattended ask-deny, and with hasUI=true and a stubbed confirm prove the prompt fires exactly once for the action, the tool executes once on accept, and is blocked on reject
Run red, record evidence in .ralph/progress.md
Implement ask handling in src/policy-engine.ts using the item-3 interaction grant (confirm at tool_call.guard with noUiOutcome=deny); run npm run verify green

items.description: Hard-deny is top-ranked, unapprovable, and unrelaxable: hard-deny outranks allow, ask, and deny; no confirm prompt is shown for it; no rule from any layered rule source inside the provider config relaxes it; the full allow < ask < deny < hard-deny lattice is deterministic.
steps: Write failing tests at the direct dispatch seam: a hard-deny-matched tool_call is blocked even when allow and ask rules also match, and a stubbed confirm is never invoked for it

Add a layered-source case inside the provider's own config (project-file layering is SLICE-0010, out of scope): an allow rule for the same tool in a second rule source does not relax the hard-deny — composition is monotonic
Add a full-lattice determinism case now that all four severities exist: decision, winning rule id, and reason identical under rules-array and object-key reordering
Run red, record evidence in .ralph/progress.md, implement the hard-deny short-circuit, run npm run verify green

items.description: Host-final approval fingerprints: an interactive approval is a SHA256 fingerprint over canonical JSON of the exact Host-final tool name and full input, stored Host-lived, single-use, expiring (default TTL 300s), validated and consumed at tool_call.internalFinal; any Host-owned input change after approval denies without re-asking.
steps: Write failing tests at the scripted agent turn seam: an approved elevated tool_call executes exactly once (marker evidence); replaying the identical call afterwards requires a new approval (single-use); an approval past its TTL (fake timers or injected clock) is not honored

Add the intra-dispatch case at the direct dispatch seam: a module transform changes the input between guard approval and internalFinal — the fingerprint misses, the call is denied, and the confirm stub is not invoked a second time
Run red, record evidence in .ralph/progress.md
Implement the fingerprint store (compute at tool_call.guard, validate + consume over Host-final input at tool_call.internalFinal); run npm run verify green

items.description: Provider-tool parity: a tool registered by another capability provider is gated by the same rules with the same outcomes as a built-in tool at the same observed tool_call boundary. Likely verification-only — if no gating gap exists, do not invent a fix.
steps: Write a test at the scripted agent turn seam where a second provider registers a marker tool via its tools grant (reuse toolProviderSource from test/providers.test.ts) and a deny rule targets it: the provider tool never executes and the blocked outcome matches the same rule denying a built-in tool
Assert the denial reason (winning rule id, severity) is identical in shape for both; do not assert target-tool provenance inside audit records (audit provider attribution keeps its existing meaning)

If the test is red, record evidence in .ralph/progress.md and implement the gap; if it is green because all tool_calls already flow through the same dispatch path, record that finding in .ralph/progress.md and keep the test as the parity pin — this item is then test-only
Run npm run verify green

items.description: Agent-first denial and ask messages: every denial (and unattended ask-resolved-to-deny, once item 4 exists) surfaces the matched rule id, its scope, and a concrete remedy in the model-visible tool output, following Pi tool-output conventions, with no universal-enforcement or OS-containment claims.
steps: Write failing tests at the scripted agent turn seam asserting the blocked tool call's model-visible tool result contains the matched rule id, the rule's scope, and its concrete remedy text, and contains no claim of OS-level or universal enforcement
Cover a plain deny message and, if item 4 has landed, an unattended ask-resolved-to-deny message; also assert the direct dispatch reason string carries the same rule id and severity
Run red, record evidence in .ralph/progress.md
Implement the message formatter in src/policy-engine.ts consuming the rule's id/scope/remedy fields; run npm run verify green
